portfolio.name: Fozayel Ibn Ayaz
portfolio.role: Full-stack developer · data analyst · WordPress builder
portfolio.summary: I notice the empty state, the missing tracking event, and the customer who stopped replying. Then I build the useful next step.
portfolio.longerSummary: I work at the seam between a polished interface and the system that has to keep it honest — code, data, content, QA, and the unglamorous details that make a product trustworthy.

projects.title: AI YouTube Command Center
projects.summary: A command center for creators who want the story behind the numbers, not another pile of charts.
projects.what: Built an OAuth-connected Next.js dashboard across 12+ YouTube Analytics endpoints, plus an AI assistant with 30+ function-calling tools for on-demand channel insights. Added smart notifications, weekly and monthly digests, and production CI.
projects.how: Typed API boundaries, scheduled GitHub Actions jobs, server-side data aggregation, and a UI that turns retention, search terms, views, and subscriber movements into decisions you can actually make.
projects.outcome: Production-grade creator intelligence, without the spreadsheet archaeology.

projects.title: Eagle 3D Streaming BI Hub
projects.summary: A single operational view for KPIs, customers, revenue, and anomalies that should not wait for Monday.
projects.what: Built a secure 10-page analytics platform unifying KPI scraping, YouTube OAuth analytics, customer success tracking, and a payment ledger for new versus recurring revenue.
projects.how: Python and Streamlit on top of MongoDB, with a four-times-daily automated pipeline, 15-minute anomaly detection, cookie-based authentication, and 16 alert types routed through Telegram.
projects.outcome: Less tab switching. Faster decisions. Better questions in the room.

projects.title: EuroEdge Admission Group
projects.summary: A clearer digital front door for a UK-based international student consultancy.
projects.what: Created a multi-page WordPress and Elementor architecture covering study destinations, English and IELTS courses, visa and admission services, and a partner-university network.
projects.how: Started with the content model, then shaped navigation, reusable page sections, conversion points, and a layout system that lets a non-technical team keep the site alive.
projects.outcome: More clarity before the first consultation.

projects.title: AEG Fournitures Storefront
projects.summary: A French WooCommerce storefront for the very serious business of moving and packing supplies.
projects.what: Designed the experience end-to-end in Figma and built the full WordPress storefront solo — catalog structure, category system, product listings, and checkout.
projects.how: Translated a visual system into reusable templates, balanced dense product information with quick scanning, and owned the last-mile details from concept through launch.
projects.outcome: A storefront that gets out of the way of the shopping.

projects.title: Things Worth Buying
projects.summary: A product-discovery site for recommendations that earn the click.
projects.what: Built a modular Next.js affiliate website with clean product presentation, environment-based configuration, and a Dockerized deployment setup.
projects.how: Separated content from components, kept the configuration portable between environments, and optimized the browsing experience around quick trust and fast loading.
projects.outcome: Curiosity, curated — with fewer mystery tabs.

projects.title: Moving & Storage Sites
projects.summary: Ongoing page development for two live businesses where reliability beats reinvention.
projects.what: Extended page templates, layout sections, and content structure across demenagement-blondeau.com and demenagementgauvin.com as part of continued WordPress development support.
projects.how: Worked within an existing ecosystem, learned its constraints, then improved pages without breaking the business underneath them — the underrated superpower.
projects.outcome: Small improvements, shipped safely, over time.
